answers.children: Yes — Collies are good with children because their gentle temperament and intelligence let them play with a softness that matches the size and movements of little ones. The herding instinct leads them to nudge or circle kids to keep the group together yet their loyal nature makes them patient and protective without roughness. Their sensitivity means they do best in calm homes where harsh tones are avoided. (PawLabs child-friendly score: 8/10)
answers.other-pets: Yes — Collies generally get along with other pets thanks to their gentle disposition and low prey drive as livestock herders rather than hunters. They may attempt to herd cats or smaller dogs by circling them but their intelligence allows them to learn boundaries quickly when introduced thoughtfully. Loyal bonding means they integrate best with household animals once trust is established.
answers.exercise: Collies need one to two hours of daily exercise such as long walks or purposeful hikes that engage their herding instincts on uneven ground. Without enough activity and mental stimulation their intelligence leads to restlessness or chewing household items as they seek tasks. Their moderate energy level means they settle once the mind and body are occupied rather than demanding constant running.
answers.shedding: Yes — Collies shed heavily especially during seasonal changes because their long double coat traps loose undercoat that then spreads through the house. The flowing mane and feathering around the legs and tail require regular removal of dead hair to prevent mats in the thick undercoat. This coat type from their Scottish origins means daily attention stops loose fur from accumulating on furniture and clothing.
answers.hypoallergenic: No breed is hypoallergenic and the Collie is not one of those commonly suggested for allergy sufferers because its long double coat sheds profusely and releases dander into the environment. The dense undercoat and long outer layer typical of Scottish herding stock hold onto particles that become airborne during grooming or seasonal blows. Their graceful build does not change the fact that the coat demands frequent vacuuming from owners sensitive to dog hair.
answers.training: Yes — Collies are easy to train because their exceptional intelligence and trainability allow them to master complex tasks with minimal guidance just as they once herded livestock on Scottish moors. Sensitivity to harsh tones means positive consistent methods work best and their loyal nature makes them eager to please once they understand the job. This biddability turns training into an engaging mental workout.
answers.lifespan: Collies live 12-14 years. Their health robustness is supported by the agile build developed for navigating rugged Scottish terrain yet sensitivity to stressful environments can affect overall wellbeing if harmony is not maintained. The long double coat requires grooming that keeps skin healthy while their intelligent herding background rewards routines that include both physical activity and mental challenges to sustain vitality across the years.
answers.size: Collies reach 50-75 lb and stand 22-26 in tall at the shoulder. This medium graceful build with a flowing long coat gives them an elegant presence that feels substantial when they lean against a leg for reassurance yet light enough to move through a home without knocking items over. Their proportions reflect the agility once needed to control flocks across uneven ground.
answers.barking: Collies do not bark a lot because their intelligence and herding background make them alert yet measured rather than noisy watchdogs. They tend to bark mainly when they sense a need to gather or direct the family as they would livestock and their loyal gentle nature keeps vocalisations purposeful instead of frequent. This moderate tendency suits homes that value a quiet but responsive companion.
answers.apartment: Yes — Collies can live in an apartment provided they receive sufficient daily exercise and mental stimulation to match their intelligence. Their moderate energy and ability to settle indoors once needs are met allow them to adapt to smaller spaces without destruction though their long coat means extra cleaning for shed hair. Sensitivity to chaotic environments makes calm routines essential for contentment.
answers.first-time: No — Collies are not the easiest first dog because their sensitivity to harsh tones requires an owner who can provide patient consistent guidance without frustration. The exceptional intelligence demands mental stimulation to prevent boredom while the herding instinct may lead to circling children or pets if not channelled. Their loyal yet reserved nature with strangers adds a layer that benefits from experienced handling.
